claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding provide adequate oxidation resistance in normal subcritical-water conditions.
Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
High-temperature exposure accelerates Cr–Zr interdiffusion at the coating/substrate interface.
Accelerated Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of the Cr coating in high-temperature steam.
Trace yttrium can be co-deposited into a Cr coating with a uniform distribution.
Yttrium added to the Cr coating will preferentially segregate to Cr grain boundaries.
Initial oxidation of the Y-doped Cr coating will form finely dispersed, stable Y-rich oxide nanoparticles.
Y-rich oxide nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries in the Cr coating.
Grain-boundary pinning by Y-rich oxide precipitates will lower Cr-atom mobility.
Suppressing grain-boundary diffusion pathways will reduce the oxidation rate of the coating.
Suppressing grain-boundary mobility will reduce interfacial mixing of Cr and Zr.
The Y-doped coating will have lower oxidation weight gain than an unmodified Cr coating.
The Y-doped coating will exhibit slower Cr–Zr interdiffusion than an unmodified Cr coating.
The Y-doped coating will retain better mechanical integrity than an unmodified Cr coating.
The predicted improvements will occur under both normal subcritical-water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam conditions.
The applicable normal-operation boundary is approximately 300°C subcritical water for extended exposure.
The applicable accident boundary extends to 800°C steam for tens to hundreds of hours.
The Y-doped Cr intervention is validated from approximately 300°C subcritical water to 800°C high-temperature steam for tens to hundreds of hours.
The optimum yttrium dose and its effect on long-term coating performance remain undetermined.
Uniform incorporation of yttrium during scaled deposition remains an open challenge.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that performance is validated over the specified temperature and duration range, while the uncertainty field says that long-term performance still requires experimental validation.

The intervention calls for process parameters optimized for uniform yttrium incorporation, but the uncertainty field states that the optimum yttrium dose and scalable uniform incorporation are not yet established.
